question.prompt: The data set \([6, 19, 33, 33, 39,\) \(41,\) \(41,\) \(43,\) \(51,\) \(57]\) has median \(Q_2 = 40,\) first quartile \(Q_1 = 33,\) and third quartile \(Q_3 = 43.\) An outlier in a data set is a value that is more than \(1.5\) times the interquartile range below the first quartile \((Q_1)\) or more than \(1.5\) times the interquartile range above the third quartile \((Q_3),\) where the interquartile range is defined as \(Q_3 - Q_1.\) How many outliers does this data set have?

solutions.title: Calculate the outlier cutoffs
solutions.explanation:
The given quartiles determine the two outlier cutoffs. First calculate the interquartile range and its \(1.5\) multiple:
\[
Q_3-Q_1=43-33=10,\qquad 1.5\cdot10=15.
\]
An outlier must therefore be less than
\[
33-15=18
\]
or greater than
\[
43+15=58.
\]
Only \(6\) is below \(18\), and no data value exceeds \(58\). There is \(\boxed{1}\) outlier, choice \(\text{B}\).
